title: 16-Week Return to Strength
subtitle: Cervical Spondylosis (C5-6) recovery → progressive resistance training + light running

the_c6_connection.title: Where You Are Now — From Symptom Relief to Rebuilding
the_c6_connection.content: The pins and needles are gone, which means the C6 nerve root that your C5-6 spondylosis was irritating has calmed down. That's the milestone that changes everything: the job is no longer to chase pain away, it's to rebuild capacity. This plan progressively reloads your whole body in the gym while keeping your neck in safe, neutral positions and continuing to load the elbow tendon. Daily chin tucks stay in as cheap insurance — they keep the nerve root decompressed so the symptoms don't return as the weights get heavier. You're self-guiding this now, so the warning signs below are your safety net: respect them and you can train hard and confidently.

phases.name: Reload
phases.focus: Safely reintroduce loading; neutral-neck, machine-based strength
principles: Never push through sharp, radiating, or tingling symptoms — that is the one hard rule
Neutral neck on everything: eyes forward, never crane or look up under load
Leave 3–4 reps in the tank — this phase is about pattern and tolerance, not maxing out
Keep the daily chin-tuck habit; it protects the C6 nerve as you reload
Walking is the only cardio — running starts in Phase 2
phases.nutrition: Eat to support recovery and lean muscle: roughly maintenance calories with ~1.6–2.0 g protein per kg bodyweight. A small deficit is fine if fat loss is a goal, but don't under-fuel your lifts.
avoid: Heavy barbell back squats and straight-bar deadlifts (use machines, goblet & trap bar)
Looking up or forcefully extending the neck under load

phases.name: Build
principles: Progress load gradually — add weight only when reps stay crisp and symptom-free
Running is light and secondary: easy effort, 2×/week, respect a 10% weekly increase
Monitor neck and elbow the day after every session, not just during
The landmine press is still your overhead — vertical pressing is reintroduced later
phases.nutrition: Continue adequate protein. Add a little extra carbohydrate on run days for energy.

phases.name: Strength
phases.focus: Heavier compounds, cautious overhead, full elbow loading
principles: Heavier loads (≈5–8 reps) on the main lifts — bracing and neutral neck become non-negotiable
Reintroduce overhead pressing SEATED and light; drop it instantly if any neck symptoms appear
Cervical and elbow work drop to a 2×/week maintenance dose
Runs become easy continuous efforts — comfort over pace
phases.nutrition: Fuel the heavier training. Keep protein high to support strength gains and tendon health.

phases.name: Perform
phases.focus: Maintain strength, auto-regulate, sustainable light running
principles: Auto-regulate by reps-in-reserve — train hard on good days, ease off on stiff ones
Overhead and full lifts are back if they stay symptom-free
Keep a comfortable ~25-min light run twice a week for cardio and bodyweight management
Neck and elbow work continue at a minimal maintenance dose — never drop them entirely
phases.nutrition: Eat at maintenance to hold your gains, or a slight deficit if fat loss is still a goal. Protein stays high.

warning_signs.sign: Pins, needles, numbness or tingling returning in the arm or fingers
warning_signs.action: STOP the session. This is the C6 nerve flaring — back off loading for a few days, return to gentle chin tucks, and if it persists >48h or worsens, see a doctor before training again.

warning_signs.sign: Sharp shooting pain down the arm
warning_signs.action: STOP immediately. Suggests nerve compression. Rest and book a physio/doctor review before loading the upper body again.

warning_signs.sign: Neck pain that worsens the day AFTER training
warning_signs.action: Reduce load and volume next session and recheck your neck position. If it continues 3+ days, see a physio.

warning_signs.sign: Lateral elbow pain that lingers >24h after loading
warning_signs.action: Drop back to isometric holds and lighter eccentrics for a week before progressing the tendon again.

warning_signs.sign: Knee or shin pain during or after running
warning_signs.action: Stop running, return to walking, and check your easy pace is truly conversational. Strength is the priority anyway.

warning_signs.sign: Any new neurological symptoms (dizziness, headaches, balance, weakness)
warning_signs.action: Stop all training and see a doctor before continuing.

ergonomic_checklist: Monitor at eye level (laptop stand + external keyboard)
Feet flat on the floor or a footrest, elbows at ~90° when typing
Take a posture break every 30–45 min (5 chin tucks + 5 shoulder rolls)
Use a vertical mouse to reduce wrist extension and elbow strain
Keep frequently used items within reach — no repeated overhead reaching
Do your chin tucks before every gym session as part of the warm-up
